skill.name: standup-formatter
skill.description: Formats daily, team, and project status notes into concise standup updates with Done, Today, and Blockers sections.
skill.summary: Turn work activity into clear standup updates for daily team coordination.
skill.author: ChaiWithJai

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences in SKILL.md. I found no shell execution instructions, prompt injection text, or semantic evidence of malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Daily status updates often become too long or vague for fast team coordination. This skill turns work notes into concise standup reports with clear outcomes, focus items, and blockers.
actual_capabilities: Formats updates into Done, Today, and Blockers sections.
Supports individual, team, and project standup formats.
Guides intake by timeframe and source data type.
Encourages concise written updates with three to five bullets.
Provides separate guidance for async and spoken standups.
Includes templates for individual and team status summaries.
limitations: Does not fetch git history, calendar events, or ticket data by itself.
Requires the user to provide accurate work activity details.
Does not replace project management or incident tracking tools.
May need team-specific conventions added by the user.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Personal Daily Standup
use_cases.description: Convert rough notes into a short update for yesterday, today, and blockers.

use_cases.title: Summarize Team Status
use_cases.description: Organize multiple teammate updates into a consistent team standup format.

use_cases.title: Report Project Progress
use_cases.description: Turn project activity into a focused update that highlights outcomes and dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Format My Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Format these notes into a concise individual standup: [paste notes]. Use Done, Today, and Blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Async Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an async standup for [date] from these notes: [paste notes]. Keep it clear and include useful links.

prompt_templates.title: Combine Team Updates
prompt_templates.prompt: Format these teammate updates into a team standup. Group by person and highlight blockers that need follow-up: [paste updates].

prompt_templates.title: Refine for Stakeholders
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn this project activity into a standup-style stakeholder update. Emphasize outcomes, current focus, dependencies, and risks: [paste activity].

output_examples.input: Merged the auth pull request, reviewed payment API notes, and need backend confirmation on webhook fields.
output_examples.output: Done: Merged the user auth pull request. Today: Review payment API integration details. Blockers: Need backend confirmation on webhook fields.

output_examples.input: Team notes from Alex, Priya, and Sam with mixed completed work, current focus, and one dependency.
output_examples.output: A team standup grouped by person, with each update reduced to Done, Today, and Blockers.

output_examples.input: Weekly project notes covering shipped work, planned testing, and a design decision waiting on approval.
output_examples.output: A project status update that highlights completed outcomes, near-term focus, and the pending design approval.

best_practices: Provide outcome-focused notes instead of long activity logs.
Call out blockers with the specific help or decision needed.
Mention whether the update is for async writing or a spoken standup.
anti_patterns: Do not include every meeting or minor task if it does not affect coordination.
Do not mark blockers as none when a dependency is unresolved.
Do not use the skill as a substitute for detailed project documentation.

faq.question: Can this skill create individual standups?
faq.answer: Yes. It formats personal updates into Done, Today, and Blockers sections.

faq.question: Can it summarize a whole team?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize multiple teammate updates under each person.

faq.question: Does it collect git or calendar data automatically?
faq.answer: No. It asks about possible source data, but the user must provide the details.

faq.question: Is it better for written or spoken standups?
faq.answer: It supports both. Written updates can include more detail, while spoken updates should stay shorter.

faq.question: Can it include blockers?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights blockers and encourages specific requests for help.

faq.question: Does it support weekly updates?
faq.answer: Yes. The intake allows daily, weekly, and custom timeframes.
